verdict.summary: You can make sandbox credentials yourself in minutes, but they only work against Gusto's demo environment. Real (production) Gusto data needs a Production Pre-Approval, a Security Review that asks for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 or a long controls questionnaire, and a QA review. Only established business software serving shared customers is accepted, and early-stage products are turned away.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours for the sandbox. Several days to assemble the security documents, Partner Checklist, tutorial video and marketing materials.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min (sandbox demo company only, no production account)
verdict.approval_wait: Several weeks (reported by third parties: about 1-2 weeks for the Pre-Approval response, 1 to several weeks for the Security Review, plus QA). Gusto publishes no official timeline, and there is no fast track.

steps.title: Confirm you qualify as a Gusto partner
steps.detail: The Gusto API is restricted to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners. Gusto looks for business software in categories such as accounting, ATS, performance, time tracking and business operations that serves shared customers. Early-stage products and customers connecting only their own company are not supported. If you only need your own company's data, look at Gusto's CLI or hosted MCP server instead.
gotchas: Gusto says production access is not a formality and not all applications are approved.

steps.title: Sign up at the Gusto Developer Portal
steps.detail: Create an account at dev.gusto.com, accept the terms of service and complete the Organization setup. You also need this account to submit the Pre-Approval application later.

steps.title: Create an Application and set the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the portal, create an Application to get your sandbox client_id and secret. You must enter at least one redirect URI, and you can add more. Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Wildcards and URIs with fragments (#) are not allowed.
You can edit demo redirects in the Applications tab, but production redirect changes require emailing Gusto.

steps.title: Create a demo company and invite teammates
steps.detail: Create a demo company. It comes pre-filled with employees and past payrolls, and you will connect it over OAuth. Invite teammates from the Organizations tab.

steps.title: Run a test authorization against the sandbox
steps.detail: Enter the sandbox client_id and secret in a Composio auth config and authorize as the demo company's admin. The flow uses /oauth/authorize (response_type=code, state) and a JSON POST to /oauth/token. Authorization codes expire after 10 minutes.
gotchas: Sandbox keys only work on api.gusto-demo.com. Check that the Composio toolkit can target the demo host (not verified).
Only primary or full-access admins can authorize, and each token covers one company.

steps.title: Submit the Production Pre-Approval application
steps.detail: Fill in the Pre-Approval form (a Qualtrics form linked from Gusto's introduction docs) while logged into your Developer Portal account. Gusto strongly recommends getting approval before you build. Without it, Gusto gives no implementation support, no QA review and no production keys.

steps.title: Wait for the Partnerships review
steps.detail: Gusto's Partnerships team reviews the Pre-Approval first. Third parties report a response in about 1-2 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare the Security Review package
steps.detail: Gather current audits (SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 + SOA, or PCI DSS), penetration test reports, security and privacy policies, and security and incident-response contacts. Without a formal audit you must answer a long controls questionnaire covering MFA, encryption, a bug bounty, a privacy policy and more. An agent can draft the policies and questionnaire answers, but you supply the audit reports and sign off.
gotchas: The review is paused until you answer any request for more information.

steps.title: Wait for the GRC Security Review
steps.detail: After Pre-Approval, Gusto's GRC team runs the Security Review, which may involve VISO Trust. Estimates range from about one week (Merge) to several weeks (Finch), with no fast track.

steps.title: Complete the Partner Checklist and QA review
steps.detail: Approved partners get a Partner Checklist to fill in and send to Gusto for QA review. The portal also asks for a recorded tutorial video and marketing materials. All testing happens in the demo environment.

steps.title: Receive production keys and register the production redirect
steps.detail: Gusto Developer Relations issues production keys in the portal and assigns scopes based on your use case. To set or change the production redirect URI, email Gusto with your Composio callback URL.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Switch Composio to production credentials and check token handling
steps.detail: Replace the sandbox credentials with the production ones in your Composio auth config, then check the granted scopes in the Developer Portal. Access tokens last 2 hours. Refresh tokens are single-use, and the refresh call also needs redirect_uri and client_secret. Avoid concurrent refreshes, and stay under 200 requests/min per grant.

blockers.cause: Gusto only accepts partners building for shared customers in supported categories, and it excludes early-stage products and self-connections.
blockers.fix: Check eligibility first. If you only need your own company, use Gusto's MCP server or CLI, or Composio's managed app if one exists.

blockers.symptom: Security Review stalls or is put on hold
blockers.cause: Missing audits or pen test reports, or unanswered requests for more information.
blockers.fix: Have SOC 2 / ISO 27001 reports or complete controls-questionnaire answers ready, and reply to GRC requests quickly.

blockers.cause: The call is outside the scopes Gusto assigned to your app.
blockers.fix: Check the granted scopes in the Developer Portal and email developer@gusto.com for more.

blockers.cause: The keys you get at first only work on api.gusto-demo.com.
blockers.fix: Point to the demo host until Gusto issues production keys.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails and the connection breaks
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens are single-use, so concurrent refreshes invalidate each other.
blockers.fix: Lock the token row during refresh and always store the newly returned pair.

blockers.symptom: A user cannot authorize, or only one company connects
blockers.cause: Only primary or full-access admins can authorize, and each token covers one company.
blockers.fix: Have an admin authorize, once per company.

blockers.cause: You cannot edit production redirect URIs yourself.
blockers.fix: Email Gusto to register the Composio callback URL for the production app.

composio.note: We couldn't confirm whether Composio has a managed Gusto OAuth app (the lookup failed). Check the Composio dashboard. Gusto issues production credentials only to approved partners after Pre-Approval, Security Review and QA, so if Composio has a managed app, it is the only quick path to real Gusto data. Bring your own app only if you are an eligible partner willing to go through weeks of review. Your own sandbox credentials (api.gusto-demo.com) are self-serve right away for testing.

evidence.claim: Gusto API access is restricted to App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners.
evidence.quote: The Gusto API is currently restricted to Gusto App Integration and Embedded Payroll partners.

evidence.claim: Production access is gated by Pre-Approval and Security Review, and not all applications are approved.
evidence.quote: Production access is gated, and not all applications are approved. Production Pre-Approval is not a formality.

evidence.claim: Without approval, Gusto gives no implementation support, no QA and no production keys.
evidence.quote: Without that approval, we cannot provide implementation support, QA review, or issue production keys.

evidence.claim: A Developer Portal account is required to complete the Pre-Approval application (a Qualtrics form).
evidence.quote: You must have a Developer Portal account to complete the application.

evidence.claim: Gusto does not currently support early-stage products or customers connecting their own account.
evidence.quote: Early-stage products still establishing a track record of serving small businesses.

evidence.claim: Sign up, set up the Organization, then create an Application with at least one redirect URI to get sandbox keys.
evidence.quote: To create an application, you will need to provide at least one(1) redirect URI.

evidence.claim: No wildcard or fragment redirect URIs. Production redirect changes require emailing Gusto.
evidence.quote: OAuth2 does not support wildcard URIs or URIs with fragments (e.g #).

evidence.claim: Create a demo company to test OAuth. Teammates are invited from the Organizations tab.
evidence.quote: After you create an application you will need to create a demo company

evidence.claim: The keys you get at first only work in the api.gusto-demo.com sandbox, and there are no production test accounts.
evidence.quote: Gusto is unable to provide production test accounts. All testing, both pre- and post-launch, must take place in our demo environment.

evidence.claim: Production keys require QA plus approved Pre-Approval, and the Partner Checklist is submitted for review.
evidence.quote: Gusto requires a quality review ("QA") and an approved Production Pre-Approval application for all builds using our API before we issue production keys.

evidence.claim: Gusto assigns scopes at review, and out-of-scope production calls are rejected.
evidence.quote: Any API call made outside of your assigned scope in production will be rejected.

evidence.claim: Scopes follow a resource:action pattern such as employees:read.
evidence.quote: Gusto uses scopes that refer to the resource they grant access to, followed by the action on that resource they allow (e.g. `employees:read`).

evidence.claim: PHI benefits data needs the company_benefits:read:phi scope.
evidence.quote: Benefits containing PHI are only visible to applications with the `company_benefits:read:phi` scope.

evidence.claim: The Security Review asks for audits, pen tests, policies and contacts, or a controls questionnaire.
evidence.quote: All current security related audits and supporting documentation

evidence.claim: Partnerships reviews the Pre-Approval first, then GRC runs the Security Review.
evidence.quote: Our Partnerships team will review your application and if approved, our GRC team will then kick off your Security Review.

evidence.claim: Finch reports the review takes several weeks with no fast track.
evidence.quote: this process can take several weeks once you have confirmed you have the security requirements in place. There is no fast track process for this review.

evidence.claim: Prismatic reports Gusto typically responds to production access requests in 1-2 weeks.
evidence.quote: Gusto reviews the request and typically responds within 1–2 weeks

evidence.claim: Merge reports the security review typically takes about a week.
evidence.quote: The security review will typically take one week.

evidence.claim: Authorize and token endpoints are on api.gusto.com, and authorization codes expire in 10 minutes.
evidence.quote: Expiration Time: 10 minutes

evidence.claim: Access tokens last 2 hours, and refresh tokens never expire but are single-use.
evidence.quote: Expiration Time: Never (invalid after one use)

evidence.claim: Only primary or full-access admins can authorize, and tokens are per company.
evidence.quote: Only primary admins or full access admins on the Gusto account can enable and authenticate a new application’s access

evidence.claim: Avoid token refresh race conditions.
evidence.quote: Care should be taken to avoid token refresh race conditions.

evidence.claim: The rate limit is 200 requests per minute per OAuth grant.
evidence.quote: The Gusto API rate limit is currently 200 requests per minute.

evidence.claim: Portal onboarding covers accepting terms, creating an app, the checklist, a tutorial video and marketing materials.
evidence.quote: Accept the terms of service, set up your account, and create an application to get your unique set of Gusto API keys.

evidence.claim: Gusto's hosted MCP server uses OAuth with PKCE and DCR, outside the partner gate.
evidence.quote: Authentication is OAuth with PKCE required

evidence.claim: Probes of dev.gusto.com and the authorize endpoint were blocked, so behaviour was not verified live.
After approval Gusto sets up production credentials. Unified API platforms have a partner path.
evidence.quote: we will notify the Unified API platform of your approval and begin the production setup and onboarding process
